capitals.name: Daik (Lingga)
capitals.note: Infobox: royal capital 1824-1900; the text has the court at Daik from 1788. The royal palace stood on Penyengat island off Tanjung Pinang; Tanjung Pinang was the administrative capital 1824-1900 (infobox).

rulers.name: Abdul Rahman Muazzam Shah
rulers.note: Table 1818-1832; the infobox gives 1819-1832. Proclaimed sultan on 27 November 1822 after the regalia were seized (page).

rulers.name: Mahmud IV
rulers.note: Table 1842-1857; the infobox gives 1835-1857. Deposed by the Dutch on 7 October 1857 while in Singapore.

rulers.name: Abdul Rahman II
rulers.note: Table 1883-1911, crowned 13 October 1883 (text); the infobox gives 1885-1911. Deposed and exiled to Singapore in 1911.

correction.text: 1820-1823: no Riau-Lingga Sultanate yet; the land is the Dutch-dominated half of the undivided Johor-Riau sultanate (Dutch paramountcy by the agreement of 27 November 1818; Abdul Rahman proclaimed sultan 27 November 1822)

keyframe_review.note: The page founds the sultanate from the Dutch-controlled southern part of Johor-Riau at the Anglo-Dutch partition of 1824, so a Riau-Lingga row for 1820-1823 is early; the land belongs to Johor-Riau (sultanate-of-johor dossier). Cliopatria's shape here (101,870 km2) also reaches the whole of Riau province on the Sumatran mainland (see the 1824 verdict).

keyframe_review.note: The Cliopatria shape is 327 cells (about 82,700 km2 by the gazetteer, 103,825 km2 in shapes.csv) and contains 297 cells of the whole Riau province on the Sumatran mainland. The page lists only four mainland districts in Indragiri (and an enclave at Kateman); it says nothing of Siak, Kampar or Rokan, so those are not drawn here. The infobox gives no area, so no ratio could be taken; the island land is a small fraction of the Cliopatria figure.

ledger.note: 1824: the Dutch half of Johor-Riau becomes the Riau-Lingga Sultanate, seat Daik on Lingga. The page dates the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 to 2 June 1824 and founds the sultanate from the Dutch-controlled southern part (closely paraphrased). The treaty page dates signing to 17 March 1824, Dutch ratification to 2 June and the exchange of ratifications to 8 June 1824.

ledger.note: 1824: the southern, Dutch-sphere half of the Johor-Riau sultanate passes to the new Riau-Lingga Sultanate. The page lists the dominions (Riau, Lingga, Tudjuh archipelagos; Batam, Bintan, Karimun, Singkep, Natuna, Anambas; Igal, Gaung, Reteh and Mandah in Indragiri); the Anglo-Dutch treaty page binds the British not to treat with rulers on the Karimun islands, Batam, Bintan, Lingga 'or any of the other islands south of the strait of Singapore'. The Johor dossier records the matching loss.

ledger.note: 1824: the sultanate is a Dutch protectorate from its foundation. Infobox 'Status: Dutch protectorate'; the 1818 agreement made 'the Dutch ... the paramount leaders of the Johor-Riau Sultanate', and the page calls the sultan deposed in 1857 the Dutch 'vassal'. Recorded on the vassal's side (overlord as counterpart). The dutch-east-indies dossier should mirror it for 1824-1911 in place of its 1857 gain. Added by the reviewer 2026-10-19.

1857: the Dutch depose Sultan Mahmud IV; Sulaiman Badrul Alam Shah II is sultan from that year and the sultanate continues. 'The Dutch therefore deposed him on 7 October 1857 while he was in Singapore.' Cliopatria's row ends in 1856 and the Dutch East Indies dossier takes the land in 1857; the page shows a continuing sultanate to 1911.
1900: the royal seat moves from Daik to Tanjung Pinang. Infobox: Daik royal capital 1824-1900; Tanjung Pinang 'royal and administrative capital 1900-1911'.

notes: Page budget 2 (Riau-Lingga article, Anglo-Dutch Treaty). (1) Life span: the page founds the sultanate in 1824 and abolishes it on 11 February 1911, so the dossier runs 1824..1911 against Cliopatria's 1820..1856. (2) Disagreement with the Dutch East Indies dossier (another group), which takes Cliopatria's Riau-Lingga land into the Indies in 1857 at low confidence; this page shows the sultanate lasting until 1911 under Dutch control, so the Indies dossier should draw the 1857-1911 land as a vassal (protectorate) tint, not as direct rule, and take it direct only from 1911/1913. (3) The Cliopatria shape overreaches onto the Sumatran mainland (297 cells = all of Riau province); the Siak and Indragiri sultanates there are not Riau-Lingga land on this page. (4) The infobox and the sultan table disagree on reign years (Muhammad II 1832-1835 vs 1832-1842, Mahmud IV 1835-1857 vs 1842-1857, Abdul Rahman II 1885-1911 vs 1883-1911); the table is used, the infobox noted. (5) The page mentions no war. (6) Gazetteer names needed: Daik (place, Lingga), Penyengat (place), Tembilahan (place, Indragiri Hilir); the Indragiri enclaves are given by coordinate, 103.0E 0.4S, 70 km.
